title: Rejection and Belonging in Christ
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Rejection and belonging in Christ teaches that people rejected, unwanted, or cast aside by others can find true identity, welcome, and belonging in Jesus. Human rejection does not define those whom Christ receives.
summary: Rejection and belonging in Christ teaches that people rejected, unwanted, or cast aside by others can find true identity, welcome, and belonging in Jesus. Human rejection does not define those whom Christ receives.
christFocus: Jesus Christ was rejected by men and yet became the cornerstone. He receives sinners, welcomes the outcast, and gives His people belonging in the household of God.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Rejection is a deep wound. Family, friends, churches, communities, or society may make people feel unwanted, disposable, or disqualified. Scripture speaks directly to this pain.

Christ Himself was rejected. He knows what it is to be despised and unwanted by men. Yet He is chosen and precious before God, and those who come to Him share in His welcome.

In Christ, believers receive a new belonging. They are children of God, members of His household, living stones in His people, and accepted by grace.

This belonging does not erase the pain of human rejection immediately, but it gives a stronger identity. The believer is not defined by who pushed him away, but by the Savior who received him.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Rejected people often carry lies about their worth. They may assume being unwanted by people means being unwanted by God. This doctrine confronts that lie with the welcome of Christ.

It also calls the church to reflect Christ’s welcome. God’s people must not treat the wounded, poor, disabled, recovering, or socially rejected as outsiders to be tolerated.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring rejection to Christ and let His welcome speak louder than the voices that cast you aside. Receive your belonging in Him, seek faithful community, and become the kind of believer who welcomes others with the grace Christ has shown you.
